references.text: God fills Bezalel with His Spirit and with wisdom to perform artistic work, the same principle of divine wisdom given to craftsmen.
God gives wisdom in the heart to all who are skilled, to make everything the Lord has commanded, including the priestly garments.
All who are wise at heart among the people are called to come and make everything the Lord has commanded.
Women who were wise at heart spun with their hands, and everyone who had wisdom in the heart contributed to the work of the tabernacle.
God filled the craftsmen with a spirit of wisdom to perform all kinds of work, parallel to the spirit of wisdom given for the priestly garments.
The wise men whom the Lord had given wisdom and understanding in their hearts are called to carry out the sanctuary work.
Aaron's sons shall be clothed in the priestly garments and consecrated to serve as priests, the same purpose of sanctification for priestly service.
Instructions for consecrating Aaron and his sons to the priesthood for the Lord.
Aaron is clothed in the holy garments and anointed to serve as a priest, fulfilling the sanctifying purpose of the garments.
Moses clothes Aaron with the tunic and the other priestly garments as part of the ordination ceremony.
Solomon asks for a wise heart to judge the people, the same concept of divine wisdom given to the heart.
The Spirit of the Lord shall rest upon the Messiah with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, parallel to the spirit of wisdom given to the craftsmen.
God gives wisdom generously to all who ask for it, the same principle of divine wisdom given to people.
Connects the making of the holy garments (Exodus 28:3) with their actual use in the ordination ritual (Exodus 40:13).
Complements Exodus 28:3 by showing that anointing is the decisive act that completes the consecration of the priest.
Places the consecration of the priest (Ex 28:3) in the broader context of consecrating the entire tabernacle and altar.
